## Q1
The number of pixel columns divided by the number of scan lines displayed by a system is called:

## Q1 - Options
(A) Pixmap
(B) Bitmap
(C) Aspect ratio
(D) Depth

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q56

Aspect ratio is the ratio of horizontal pixels (or columns) to vertical scan lines. A bitmap/pixmap is an image representation, while depth refers to bits per pixel.

## Q2
Which of the following statements are true?<br>
A. Painters' algorithm is also called depth sort algorithm.<br>
B. Gourad shading is an interpolating shading method.<br>
C. Gourad shading is an averaging shading method.<br>
D. The Z-buffer algorithm finds the largest depth value Z.

## Q2 - Options
(A) A, B Only
(B) B, C Only
(C) C, D Only
(D) A, D Only

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q37

- **A. Painters' algorithm is also called depth sort algorithm.** — correct. The algorithm sorts polygons by depth and paints them from farthest to nearest, which is exactly why it is also known as the depth-sort algorithm.
- **B. Gourad shading is an interpolating shading method.** — correct. Gouraud shading computes intensity at each vertex and then linearly interpolates those intensity values across the surface of the polygon.
- **C. Gourad shading is an averaging shading method.** — incorrect. Averaging is only used as an intermediate step to compute a vertex normal from the surrounding polygon normals, but the shading method itself is classified by intensity interpolation, not by averaging.
- **D. The Z-buffer algorithm finds the largest depth value Z.** — incorrect. The Z-buffer algorithm keeps the smallest depth value at each pixel, since the point nearest to the viewer is the one that should be visible, not the farthest one.

So the correct statements are A and B only.

## Q3
Match List-I (Quadric surfaces) with List-II (Equations).

| List-I (Quadric Surface) | List-II (Equation) |
|---|---|
| A. One-sheeted hyperboloid | I. x²/a² + y²/b² = cz |
| B. Two-sheeted hyperboloid | II. x²/a² + y²/b² - z²/c² = 1 |
| C. Elliptic paraboloid | III. x²/a² - y²/b² = cz |
| D. Hyperbolic paraboloid | IV. z²/c² - x²/a² - y²/b² = 1 |

## Q3 - Options
(A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
(B) A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
(C) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
(D) A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q65

Each quadric surface has a distinct standard equation determined by its sign pattern and which variable stands alone.

A one-sheeted hyperboloid has two positive squared terms and one negative term equal to 1, giving x²/a² + y²/b² - z²/c² = 1, so A pairs with II.<br>
A two-sheeted hyperboloid flips this pattern with one positive term and two negative terms equal to 1, giving z²/c² - x²/a² - y²/b² = 1, so B pairs with IV.<br>
An elliptic paraboloid has two positive squared terms equal to a linear term, giving x²/a² + y²/b² = cz, so C pairs with I.<br>
A hyperbolic paraboloid has one positive and one negative squared term equal to a linear term, giving x²/a² - y²/b² = cz, so D pairs with III.

This gives A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

## Q8
Match List I with List II.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. 2-D Array Input | I. Liquid Crystal display |
| B. Transmissive device | II. Flat-bed scanner |
| C. Binary image | III. Camera |
| D. 1-D array input | IV. Ink jet printer |

## Q8 - Options
(A) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
(B) A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
(C) A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
(D) A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q67

Each item is matched by the way it captures or produces image data.

A camera's sensor captures an entire image at once as a full two-dimensional grid of pixels, making it a 2-D array input device, giving A-III.

A liquid crystal display works by modulating light that passes through its layers, which is why it is classified as a transmissive device, giving B-I.

An ink jet printer builds an image from individual dots that are either fired or not at each position, which is a binary (on/off) decision per pixel, matching binary image output, giving C-IV.

A flat-bed scanner builds its image by moving a single sensor line across the page, capturing one row (a one-dimensional array) at a time, giving D-II.

This gives the mapping A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

## Q9
Assertion (A): A Raster scan device is a CRT graphic device and can use a television monitor for display.

Reason (R): In Raster scan display the picture is composed of a series of dots. These dots are traced out as a series of horizontal lines. Television works in a similar fashion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q9 - Options

(B) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

(D) A is false but R is true

## Q9 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q87

A raster scan CRT builds its image from a series of dots traced out along horizontal scan lines, which is exactly how a television picture tube also draws its image.

That shared horizontal-line scanning mechanism is precisely why a raster scan device can reuse television display hardware, so Reason R directly explains why Assertion A is true.

## Q10
Hidden surface removal problem with minimal 3D pipeline can be solved with

## Q10 - Options
(A) Painter's algorithm
(B) Window Clipping algorithm
(C) Brute force rasterization algorithm
(D) Flood fill algorithm

## Q10 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q17

Painter's algorithm removes hidden surfaces with minimal extra pipeline machinery by simply depth-sorting polygons from farthest to nearest and drawing them in that order, so nearer surfaces naturally overwrite farther ones on the frame buffer.

Window clipping only restricts geometry to the viewport and does not resolve visibility, brute-force rasterization scan-converts polygons without any depth logic of its own, and flood fill is a region-filling technique unrelated to depth or visibility at all.

## Q11
You have eight black-and-white images taken with a 1-megapixel camera and one 8-colour image taken with an 8-megapixel camera. How much disk space in total is needed to store these images?

## Q11 - Options
(A) 1 GB
(B) 4 MB
(C) 3 MB
(D) 3 GB

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q6

A black-and-white pixel needs 1 bit, so each 1-MP image is 1,000,000 bits = 125 KB, and eight of them total about 1 MB. An 8-colour image needs 3 bits per pixel, so 8 MP x 3 bits = 24,000,000 bits = about 3 MB. Total is roughly 1 MB + 3 MB = 4 MB.

## Q14
Consider the following statements with respect to approaches to fill area on raster systems:

P. To determine the overlap intervals for scan lines that cross the area<br>
Q. To start from a given interior position and paint outward from this point until a encounter the specified boundary conditions

Select the correct answer:

## Q14 - Options
(A) P only
(B) Q only
(C) Both P and Q
(D) Neither P nor Q

## Q14 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2019 (4 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q4

Raster graphics algorithms use two standard approaches to fill interior regions:

- **P** — describes scan-line polygon filling, where intersection spans along successive scan lines intersecting polygon boundaries are calculated.
- **Q** — describes seed fill algorithms (boundary-fill and flood-fill), which start from an interior pixel and propagate outward until boundary conditions are met.

Because both P and Q are standard area-fill techniques in computer graphics, option C is correct.

## Q15
If we want to resize a 1024 × 768 pixels image to one that is 640 pixels wide with the same aspect ratio, what would be the height of the resized image?

## Q15 - Options
(A) 420 Pixels
(B) 460 Pixels
(C) 480 Pixels
(D) 540 Pixels

## Q15 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2019 (4 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q85

The aspect ratio of the original image is preserved when resizing.

Aspect Ratio = Width / Height = 1024 / 768 = 4 / 3

Given the resized width W₂ = 640 pixels:

W₂ / H₂ = 4 / 3 =&gt; H₂ = (3 / 4) \* 640 = 3 \* 160 = 480 pixels

The height of the resized image is 480 pixels.

## Q16
Consider a raster system with resolution 640 by 480. What size is frame buffer (in bytes) for this system to store 12 bits per pixel?

## Q16 - Options
(A) 450 kilobytes
(B) 500 kilobytes
(C) 350 kilobytes
(D) 400 kilobytes

## Q16 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q29

Calculating total frame buffer capacity from screen dimensions and color depth:

Total pixels = 640 \* 480 = 307,200 pixels.<br>
Each pixel requires 12 bits of storage.<br>
Total bit capacity = 307,200 \* 12 = 3,686,400 bits.

Converting to bytes:<br>
3,686,400 / 8 = 460,800 bytes.

Converting to kilobytes (using 1024 bytes per kilobyte):<br>
460,800 / 1024 = 450 kilobytes.

## Q17
Using the phong reflectance model, the strength of the specular highlight is determined by the angle between

## Q17 - Options
(A) the view vector and the normal vector
(B) the light vector and the normal vector
(C) the light vector and the reflected vector
(D) the reflected vector and the view vector

## Q17 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q84

The Phong illumination model calculates specular reflection using the cosine of the angle between the viewer's line of sight and the ideal reflection path:

I_spec = I_s \* k_s \* (R · V)^n

Here, R is the unit vector along the direction of ideal mirror reflection of the incident light, and V is the unit vector pointing toward the observer viewpoint.<br>
The highlight intensity depends directly on the angle between the reflected vector and the view vector.

## Q18
If the frame buffer has 10-bits per pixel and 8-bits are allocated for each of the R, G, and B components, then what would be the size of the color lookup table (LUT) ?

## Q18 - Options
(A) (2¹⁰ + 2²⁴) bytes
(B) (2¹⁰ + 2¹¹) bytes
(C) (2⁸ + 2⁹) bytes
(D) (2¹⁰ + 2⁸) bytes

## Q18 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q9

The size of a color lookup table equals the number of table entries multiplied by the storage required per entry.

Number of entries = 2^(bits per pixel) = 2^10 entries<br>
Bits per entry = 8 bits (R) + 8 bits (G) + 8 bits (B) = 24 bits = 3 bytes per entry

Total size in bytes:<br>
Size = 2^10 \* 3 bytes<br>
Size = 2^10 \* (1 + 2) bytes<br>
Size = 2^10 + (2^10 \* 2^1) bytes = 2^10 + 2^11 bytes.

- Option A incorrectly adds the 24-bit total color space depth to the entries.
- Option C uses 8 bits for indexing rather than 10 bits.
- Option D incorrectly computes 2^10 + 2^8.

## Q19
In 3D Graphics, which of the following statements is/are true ?

P : Back-face culling is an example of an image-precision visible-surface determination procedure.<br>
Q : Z-buffer is a 16-bit, 32-bit, or 64-bit field associated with each pixel in a frame buffer that can be used to determine the visible surfaces at each pixel.

Choose the correct answer from the code given below :<br>
Code :

## Q19 - Options
(A) Q only
(B) P and Q
(C) Neither P nor Q
(D) P only

## Q19 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q24

Visible-surface determination methods are classified into object-space precision and image-space precision.

- Statement P is false because back-face culling operates in object space by calculating polygon surface normals and dot products, making it an object-precision procedure.
- Statement Q is true because the Z-buffer algorithm stores depth values (typically 16, 24, 32, or 64 bits) per pixel in image space to resolve surface visibility.
- Therefore, only statement Q is true (Option A).

## Q20
Consider the midpoint (or Bresenham) algorithm for rasterizing lines given below :

(1) Input (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)<br>
(2) y = y1<br>
(3) d = f(x1 + 1, y1 + 1/2) //f is the implicit form of a line<br>
(4) for x = x1 to x2<br>
(5) do<br>
(6) plot(x, y)<br>
(7) if(d &lt; 0)<br>
(8) then<br>
(9) y = y + 1<br>
(10) d = d + (y1 – y2) + (x2 – x1)<br>
(11) else<br>
(12) d = d + (y1 – y2)<br>
(13) end<br>
(14) end

Which statements are true?<br>
P : For a line with slope m &gt; 1, we should change the outer loop in line (4) to be over y.<br>
Q : Lines (10) and (12) update the decision variable d through an incremental evaluation of the line equation f.<br>
R : The algorithm fails if d is ever 0.

Choose the correct answer from the code given below :<br>
Code :

## Q20 - Options
(A) Q and R only
(B) P and Q only
(C) P, Q and R
(D) P only

## Q20 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Computer Graphics: Display, Algorithms & 3D
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q83

Statements P and Q are true principles of Bresenham's rasterization algorithm, while statement R is false.

- Statement P is true because stepping along x for steep lines (slope m &gt; 1) produces discontinuous pixels, requiring the roles of x and y to swap so the loop iterates along y.
- Statement Q is true because Bresenham's method evaluates decision variable d incrementally using finite differences of the implicit line equation rather than floating-point recalculation.
- Statement R is false because when d = 0, the midpoint lies directly on the line equation, and the algorithm safely defaults to selecting either candidate pixel without failure.
- Therefore, statements P and Q only are true (Option B).
